The pharaohs used trade to accumulate wealth, which they could then use to fund their military campaigns, build grand monuments, and maintain their divine status.

The pharaohs also used trade to exert their influence over neighboring kingdoms and territories. They would often establish trade agreements, which would grant them access to valuable resources and strategic locations. This allowed them to expand their empire, secure their borders, and maintain their power.

These guilds would also provide training and support to young merchants, helping them to develop the skills and knowledge needed to succeed in the trade.
